title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: TEO'S WALL
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Teo Salinas, a fifty-year-old power lineman in El Paso, Texas.
For thirty years, he climbed poles and doodled on napkins.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: TOO OLD
segments.quote: Everybody has talent at twenty-five. The difficult thing is to have it at fifty.
segments.author: Edgar Degas
lines: Mrs. Ochoa, who runs the laundromat, saw his napkin sketch of her cat.
Her back wall got tagged every week. Paint me a mural, she said.
Teo laughed. I'm fifty.
That night, his wife Lupe stuck a postcard on the fridge, from the French painter Edgar Degas:
Everybody has talent at twenty-five. The difficult thing is to have it at fifty.
He bought the paint.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE POSTCARD
segments.quote: Just to paint a representation or design is not hard, but to express a thought in painting is.
segments.author: Edward Hopper
lines: His first sketch copied a postcard of the mountains. Pretty. And empty.
Then he read the American painter Edward Hopper:
Just to paint a representation or design is not hard, but to express a thought in painting is.
So he sketched the real block. Mrs. Ochoa. Don Chuy, the ice cream man.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE PINK SKY
segments.quote: An expert is a person who has made all the mistakes which can be made in a very narrow field.
segments.author: Niels Bohr
lines: Day one, he mixed the sky wrong. It came out the color of stomach medicine.
Abel, a retired sign painter, quoted the scientist Niels Bohr:
An expert is a person who has made all the mistakes which can be made in a very narrow field.
You're on mistake number one, Abel said. Go make the rest.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: STIFF FACES
segments.quote: Every artist dips his brush in his own soul, and paints his own nature into his pictures.
segments.author: Henry Ward Beecher
lines: But the faces looked stiff, like driver's license photos.
Lupe read him a line from Henry Ward Beecher, a famous American speaker:
Every artist dips his brush in his own soul, and paints his own nature into his pictures.
So Teo painted his mom's tamales in a window, and a tiny lineman on a pole, waving.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE CRITICS
segments.quote: Remember, a statue has never been set up in honor of a critic.
segments.author: Jean Sibelius
lines: Then the neighborhood group chat caught fire. Don Chuy said his belly was too big.
Abel quoted the Finnish composer Jean Sibelius:
Remember, a statue has never been set up in honor of a critic.
Teo shrank the belly anyway. Don Chuy said it was too small.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE TAGGER
segments.quote: The question is not what you look at, but what you see.
segments.author: Henry David Thoreau
lines: One dawn, Teo caught the tagger. Danny, nineteen, spray can in hand.
Teo almost yelled. Then he remembered Henry David Thoreau:
The question is not what you look at, but what you see.
He saw a steady hand. So he handed Danny a brush.
Now the wall stays clean, and on Saturdays they teach anyone who shows up.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Start late. Say something. Make mistakes. Paint yourself in. Ignore critics. See people.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Start late. Say something real. Make mistakes. Paint yourself in. Let critics talk. See people.
I painted my own portrait once. My wife loved the potato.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
